reviewed_proof_scopes.semantic_scope: Setting definitions (FinDist, SREV, BREV, Mechanism, REV, c*) and Theorem 1 general lower bound (> 2.1946) via Group A + Group B equal-revenue construction and deterministic two-part tariff plus concentrated bundle.

Theorem 2 universal upper bound (REV <= 1.1187*SREV + 1.367299*BREV <= 2.486*max(SREV, BREV)) and Corollary 3 bracket (2.1946 <= c* <= 2.486) via finite-support duality, layer cake, step-function Jensen weights, 4-exponential Laplace bundle bound, and kernel-verified 1D certificate.

Theorem 4 (40-item i.i.d. lower bound > 1.316) and Proposition 5 (100-item i.i.d. lower bound >= 1.324907) via truncated equal-revenue distributions, deterministic two-part tariff (entry fee 9, item price 4), and Kronecker-packed generating-function kernel verification.

model_conventions.formal_meaning: Each item marginal is a `FinDist` (finite support indexed by `Fin size` with nonnegative `val`, nonnegative `prob` summing to 1). Joint realizations `Profile D := (i : ι) → Fin (D i).size` have independent product probability `∏ i, (D i).prob (ω i)`. A direct `Mechanism ι` maps every valuation vector `v : ι → ℝ` to allocation probabilities `alloc v i ∈ [0,1]` and payment `pay v : ℝ` satisfying IC and IR over all nonnegative valuation vectors `v, v' ≥ 0`.
model_conventions.why_needed: The paper defines `FinDist`, `SREV`, `BREV`, `Mechanism`, `REV`, and `cStar` in Section 1 (Setting). Representing finite distributions via finite index tuples makes finite product expectations and suprema exact without auxiliary measure-theoretic assumptions.
model_conventions.checked_scope: All five named results in `PaperInterface.lean` consume `FinDist`, `SREV`, `BREV`, `Mechanism`, `REV`, and `cStar` directly.

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Combine 1280 Group A items (five equal-revenue types on [P_i, P_i+e]) with L^2 Group B harmonic items, verify SREV, BREV, and deterministic two-part-tariff + bundle revenue via packed generating functions and Chebyshev bounds, and take L sufficiently large.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: There exist m, D : Fin m -> FinDist, and a deterministic IC+IR mechanism M with M.rev D > 2.1946 * max(SREV D, BREV D) and REV D > 2.1946 * max(SREV D, BREV D).

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Prove finite-support master duality inequality, layer-cake representation with step-function Jensen weights, 4-exponential Laplace bundle bound via certified linear tangents, and 1846-cell directed-integer 1D analytic certificate inside the Lean kernel.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: For every finite index set ι and D : ι -> FinDist, REV D <= 1.1187 * SREV D + 1.367299 * BREV D, and for every m and D : Fin m -> FinDist, REV D <= 2.486 * max(SREV D, BREV D).

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Combine Theorem 1 (lower bound > 2.1946) and Theorem 2 (upper bound <= 2.486) with the infimum definition of c*.

Construct 40 i.i.d. items on {0, 4, ..., 13} with exact equal-revenue tails 3/(10*max(k,4)), certify SREV <= 12, BREV <= 12.151 via packed generating-function shifting loop, and deterministic two-part tariff (entry fee 9, item price 4) revenue >= 16 via mod-X^9 generating-function check.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: For m = 40, the explicit distribution F and deterministic two-part tariff (entry fee 9, item price 4) satisfy REV(F^{\otimes 40}) >= M.rev(F^{\otimes 40}) > 1.316 * max(SREV, BREV).

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Construct 100 i.i.d. items on {0, 4, ..., 13} with exact tails 3/(25*max(k,4)) for 1 <= k <= 13 and 0 for k > 13, certify SREV = 12, BREV <= 12.065329 via 1301-step shifting loop, and deterministic two-part tariff (entry fee 9, item price 4) revenue >= 15.985442 via mod-X^9 kernel check.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: The explicit 100-item i.i.d. distribution F and deterministic two-part tariff (entry fee 9, item price 4) satisfy REV / max(SREV, BREV) >= M.rev / max(SREV, BREV) >= 1.324907.
